postmortem:
# Summary

On 2026-10-30 the orders-api workload was moved from the default namespace to the new orders namespace (PR ORD-2914, deployment annotation records the change-cause). Pods started, passed their probes, and looked healthy, but every request that needed a secret from Key Vault kv-orders-prod returned HTTP 500 to customers. The token exchange between the Kubernetes service account and the user-assigned managed identity id-orders-api-prod failed because the identity's federated credential still named the old namespace. The fix was to add a second federated credential whose subject matches the new service account; impact lasted 47 minutes end to end.

## Impact

For 47 minutes (22:16 to 23:03 UTC) all /orders endpoints returned HTTP 500; the 5xx rate peaked at 41 percent. Customers could not place or view orders that required secret-backed configuration. No data was lost — requests failed closed before reaching order processing — and no other workload on the cluster was affected.

## Timeline

- 22:16 — Pager fires: orders-api 5xx spike; customer impact window opens.
- 22:18 — On-call confirms all pods are Running 1/1 in the orders namespace; probes are green, so the failure is at request time.
- 22:20 — Pod logs show Key Vault GetSecret calls failing with 403.
- 22:23 — Vault metrics for kv-orders-prod are flat: no error spike, no throttling — the vault itself is healthy.
- 22:27 — The Key Vault Secrets User role assignment for id-orders-api-prod is verified intact and unchanged since August.
- 22:32 — Attention shifts to workload identity: the projected service-account token subject changed with the namespace move.
- 22:42 — az identity federated-credential list confirms the only credential is fic-orders-api-default with subject system:serviceaccount:default:orders-api — the old namespace. Token exchange fails on the subject mismatch.
- 22:58 — A second federated credential, fic-orders-api-orders, is created for subject system:serviceaccount:orders:orders-api; the old credential is kept for the rollback window.
- 23:01 — The deployment is rollout-restarted so pods re-issue tokens.
- 23:03 — 5xx rate returns to baseline; customer impact window closes after 47 minutes.

## Root Cause

The namespace move changed the service-account identity that the workload presents (system:serviceaccount:orders:orders-api), but the federated credential on id-orders-api-prod was never updated: its subject still trusted system:serviceaccount:default:orders-api. Workload identity exchanges the pod's projected token for the identity's token only when the subjects match; with no credential matching the new subject, the exchange failed, the Key Vault SDK could not obtain a token, and every secret read surfaced as HTTP 500. The cluster's Azure RBAC data plane was verified healthy throughout — the failure predates authorization.

## Contributing Factors

- The move runbook for namespace migrations has no step covering federated credentials; the deployment, service account and DNS were all moved deliberately, and the credential was the one lifecycle object that lives outside the cluster manifest.
- Probes and startup checks pass without secrets, so an identity failure is invisible to deployment health gates.
- The token-exchange failure surfaces downstream as a Key Vault 403, which points the first responder at the vault before the identity.

## Action Items

- Extend the namespace-move runbook with an explicit federated-credential step: enumerate identities and their credential subjects before the move, and update subjects as part of the change (owner: platform team).
- Manage federated credentials as infrastructure-as-code so a namespace move cannot leave an identity without a matching subject (owner: platform team).
- Add a pre-move checklist item that greps all FIC subjects for the namespace being vacated (owner: SRE).
- Track the scheduled removal of the legacy fic-orders-api-default credential after the 48-hour rollback window (owner: on-call rotation).
